stories.headline: Brewers beat the Rays 4-1 in Game 5 to win the first World Series title in franchise history
stories.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers are World Series champions for the first time. They beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 Wednesday night at Tropicana Field to take the series 4-1, giving Milwaukee its first title since the 1957 Braves. Young ace Jacob Misiorowski threw 5 2/3 scoreless innings, allowing two hits, before leaving with a right calf cramp. Rookie Cooper Pratt drove in two runs after setting a Series rookie record with six straight hits, Jackson Chourio set a five-game Series record with 11 hits, and catcher William Contreras, who had an RBI double, was named World Series MVP. Milwaukee went 11-2 this postseason under manager Pat Murphy. Thousands of traveling fans packed the stands in St. Petersburg while 31,000 watched on the scoreboard back at American Family Field. The Rays, Mariners, Padres and Rockies are now the only franchises without a title. Milwaukee's championship parade is set for Friday.

stories.headline: Russian jet-powered drone hits trains at Dnipro station platform, killing at least 13
stories.summary: A Russian jet-powered drone hit a platform at the Dnipro railway station Thursday morning where a commuter train and a passenger train bound for Zaporizhzhia were standing, killing at least 13 people and wounding at least 13 more, Ukrainian authorities said. Ukraine's Air Force said four jet-powered drones attacked the area around 11 a.m. local time and air defenses shot down three. Ukrainian Railways said people stayed on the platform despite an air raid alert and warnings of a heightened threat. President Volodymyr Zelensky called it "a horrific Russian attack" and criticized the recent easing of sanctions on some Russian oligarchs and energy companies. The strike is the latest in a Russian campaign against Ukraine's rail network, which has forced strict new rules that often have passengers leaving trains during alerts. Overnight drone strikes also killed people in Kremenchuk and Chernihiv. The toll is still preliminary and may rise.

stories.headline: Alaska's governor orders a criminal probe into claims Peltola allies recruited a second 'Dan Sullivan' for the Senate ballot
stories.summary: Alaska Republican Gov. Mike Dunleavy has ordered the Department of Public Safety to investigate whether people aligned with Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola's campaign broke the law by helping recruit a second candidate named Dan Sullivan to run against Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan. The order follows a New York Times report on the alleged scheme. "Deliberately tricking voters into casting their ballots for someone else strikes at the integrity of our elections," Dunleavy wrote, adding that the probe will look at whether criminal charges or civil action are warranted. The ranked-choice ballot lists four candidates, including the incumbent, shown as a Republican, and a retired teacher named Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. with no party listed. Peltola and the Democrats' Senate campaign arm deny any role, and Peltola called the report "a distraction." President Trump said Peltola and the other Sullivan "should be prosecuted," and Breitbart reports the Justice Department is expanding its own investigation ahead of Tuesday's election.

stories.headline: Ship burns in the Strait of Hormuz as Iran says three tankers hit mines on the U.S.-backed southern route
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said Thursday that three oil tankers exploded and caught fire after hitting naval mines over the past 24 hours while using what it called "the unauthorized southern route" through the Strait of Hormuz, and that the ships were left stranded along the strait's southern shore. The U.S. has been steering shippers to that southern lane, which President Trump declared mine-free at the end of August, while Iran insists ships must use routes it controls closer to its coast. The IRGC said the tankers had switched off their radar and navigation systems and ignored warnings, and it blamed their owners and crews. Separately, a Pentagon official told CBS that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has fired the Pentagon's top military planner, Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, over accusations that he leaked classified information about the Iran war. Qatari mediators have given Tehran a new draft deal to end the war, with a reply expected by about Saturday, though an Iranian official called the ideas "unacceptable."

stories.headline: Trumbull's Coventry Lane neighbors fight a proposal for 84 apartments just over the Monroe line
stories.summary: Residents of Coventry Lane, a quiet Trumbull cul-de-sac of single-family homes, are organizing against a plan for two apartment buildings with 84 units on the lot behind their backyards at 1, 7 and 15 Main St. in Monroe. Owner Gold Coast Properties LLC has asked Monroe's Planning and Zoning Commission to add the site to the Main Street Development District and approve a special development district. A proposed text amendment would allow multifamily housing on lots over two acres within a mile of the Route 25 and Route 111 intersection, instead of the current 15-acre minimum. The buildings would sit more than 400 feet back from Route 25, and neighbors say the 40-plus-foot structures would bring traffic, noise, light, blasting and lower property values. They have put up "No 84 Unit Apartment Buildings" lawn signs and started a website and a Facebook group. A nearby shooting range also opposes the plan. The hearing continues Nov. 5 so the developer can revise the proposal. Trumbull First Selectman Vicki Tesoro issued a statement on the plan earlier this month.

stories.headline: Divers find the wreck of SS Cornwallis, sunk off Maine in 1944 by the U-boat that had just landed Nazi spies
stories.summary: The New Hampshire-based Nomad Exploration Team says it has found the wreck of the SS Cornwallis, a 400-foot Canadian steamship torpedoed off the Maine coast on Dec. 3, 1944. Side-scan sonar found the wreck in July, nearly 400 feet down, and later dives confirmed it after years of searching in cold water and strong currents. The ship was sunk by U-1230, the same German submarine that had secretly landed two Nazi spies in Maine four days earlier. The torpedo hit near the bow and the Cornwallis, carrying sugar and molasses from Barbados to St. John, New Brunswick, sank in about 10 minutes. Only five of the 48 people aboard survived. Built in Vancouver in 1921, the ship had already survived a 1942 torpedo attack while anchored in Barbados. A team member said the find brings renewed attention to "a largely forgotten tragedy."

stories.headline: South Korea fines Google $32 million and Apple $15.6 million and orders both to allow outside payments
stories.summary: South Korea's communications regulator, the Korea Media and Communications Commission, has found that Apple and Google broke the country's Telecommunications Business Act with their app stores. It fined Google 42.9 billion won (about $32 million) and Apple 20.81 billion won (about $15.6 million). After investigations and on-site inspections going back to 2022, the regulator said the companies forced use of their own in-app payment systems, charged a 26 percent commission on third-party payments and blocked external payments. It also said they delayed app reviews without clear reasons. It found that Apple calculated its cut on VAT-inclusive prices for Korean developers but on pre-VAT prices for overseas developers. Both companies must now accept external payments and revise their app review procedures, and Apple must stop treating domestic and foreign developers differently. Apple and Google already allow external payments in the U.S. and the EU.

stories.headline: Connecticut's free Mobile ID app for driver's licenses launches Nov. 18 and will work at TSA checkpoints
stories.summary: The Connecticut DMV says Connecticut Mobile ID, a free app that puts a secure digital version of your driver's license or state ID on your phone, launches Nov. 18 on the Apple App Store and Google Play. You'll need your physical license or ID card to set it up. At launch, TSA will accept it at participating airport checkpoints nationwide, including Bradley International and Tweed New Haven. It's meant to complement your physical card, not replace it. It can't be used with police, for voting or as a "flash pass," businesses don't have to accept it, and those that do need a compatible verification app. The Department of Consumer Protection will give businesses guidance. Gov. Ned Lamont called it "another step forward" in making state services more convenient.

stories.headline: Nikon's $13,999 Nikkor Z 120-300mm f/2.8 TC VR S is the first 120-300mm f/2.8 zoom with a built-in teleconverter
stories.summary: Nikon has fully announced the Nikkor Z 120-300mm f/2.8 TC VR S, a professional S-Line telephoto zoom for its full-frame mirrorless cameras, first teased in May. Its standout feature is a built-in 1.4x teleconverter, switched on with a lever on the barrel, which turns it into a 168-400mm f/4. That makes it a spiritual successor to Nikon's much-loved F-mount 200-400mm f/4, and no other 120-300mm f/2.8 has one. Nikon is aiming it at indoor sports like basketball and hockey, field sports like baseball, soccer and football, and wildlife. The optical design has 30 elements in 24 groups, including fluorite, Super ED, ED, SR and aspherical elements, with ARNEO and Meso Amorphous coatings against flare and a nine-blade aperture. DPReview puts the price at $13,999.

stories.headline: Maynard James Keenan says he became Tool's singer on a dare after criticizing the LA scene
stories.summary: Tool frontman Maynard James Keenan told Metal Hammer that he joined the band because someone dared him to. "Somebody challenged me when I was being critical about the things I was seeing in LA," the 62-year-old said. "It was like, 'If you think you can do better...' I knew I could. It was an accident, but I took the call and I'm going to be here a while." Tool went on to sell more than 14 million albums and win three Grammys, and Lateralus, 10,000 Days and Fear Inoculum all debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200. Keenan said the success eventually drove him out of Los Angeles, not because of fans but because of a "parade of vampires": lawyers, agents and bookers trying to profit from the band. He now lives in Jerome, Arizona, and despite hip replacement surgery in August he is back on the road with Puscifer.

stories.headline: Retired Lion Knights' Castle flags and cape are back on US Pick a Brick, but only until Nov. 1
stories.summary: The fabric pieces from the retired LEGO 10305 Lion Knights' Castle, two flags and a cape, are available again from Pick a Brick in the US as a multipack for $5.09. They are listed as Standard rather than Bestseller pieces, so the window is short. On Nov. 2, LEGO will temporarily stop US Standard orders while it moves its Pick a Brick stock to its Illinois warehouse, a process expected to take a few months. That makes the end of Sunday, Nov. 1 the firm deadline. New Classic Space and Castle elements from July's sets are coming soon after. Orders over $130 also get 40889 Build, Paint and Play free through Nov. 8 or while supplies last. Other 10305 parts, including minifigure shields, are still listed as Bestsellers.

stories.headline: Emergency declared at South Carolina's Savannah River nuclear site after a fire breaks out at its national lab
stories.summary: The Savannah River Site near Aiken, South Carolina, declared a Site Area Emergency at 5:39 p.m. Wednesday after a fire broke out at the Savannah River National Laboratory, according to the Department of Energy. The fire was put out and one employee was taken to a hospital with minor injuries, and a DOE spokesperson said no radiological contamination has been reported. As a precaution, site entrances were barricaded to incoming traffic, rail, river and air traffic near the site was restricted, and workers in affected areas who are not part of the response were told to shelter in place. Residents were advised to follow local radio and TV for instructions. The sprawling DOE complex, built in the 1950s to make tritium and plutonium for nuclear weapons, still manages nuclear materials and radioactive waste for the weapons program.

stories.headline: Minnesota prosecutor charges James O'Keefe and Cam Higby with felonies over their undercover polling-place video
stories.summary: Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty on Wednesday charged journalist James O'Keefe, 42, and conservative activist Cam Higby, 26, with felony unlawful voting and identity theft, each punishable by up to five years in prison. The charges stem from an August video O'Keefe posted of the pair entering Minneapolis polling places on primary day in Islamic garb, using fake accents and hidden cameras, to draw attention to Minnesota's voter-vouching law, which lets one registered voter vouch for the residency of up to eight recently moved voters. Prosecutors say O'Keefe "intentionally misrepresented their identities in applying for ballots," though neither complaint alleges they actually cast a vote. Moriarty, a progressive prosecutor elected in 2022, said the charges have nothing to do with the men's politics or the disguises, while supporters call it retaliation for exposing an election-security loophole days before the Nov. 3 midterms.

stories.headline: Hacker steals records on more than 41,000 DHS employees, including thousands of ICE and CBP agents
stories.summary: A hacker calling itself "Department of Peace" stole the names, job titles, phone numbers, email addresses and office locations of more than 41,000 Department of Homeland Security employees, according to TechCrunch and Wired. About 21,000 of the records belong to Customs and Border Protection staff and nearly 7,000 to ICE, with others from CISA, USCIS and Homeland Security Investigations. The hacker reportedly got in through Okta, the identity and login service DHS uses, and said "They have our information, so it's only fair that we have theirs." The data, dubbed "Icepick," was passed to the leak site DDoSecrets and also ties DHS units to surveillance tools such as the Mobile Fortify facial recognition app and PenLink phone-data software. It comes weeks after a similar theft of FBI employee and applicant data, and as DHS has been trying to shield the identities of agents carrying out immigration raids. DHS did not immediately comment.

stories.headline: Garrett Wilson says he doesn't want a trade out of New York, but admits he's frustrated as the 2-5 Jets keep losing
stories.summary: Jets star receiver Garrett Wilson shot down trade chatter on Wednesday, saying "I want to be here, man... I love it here. Do I love it more than I love winning? Nah, to be completely honest, but I'm hopeful." Wilson had just two catches for 26 yards on three targets in Sunday's 28-25 loss to the previously winless Dolphins, and TV cameras caught him shouting on the sideline toward Geno Smith and passing-game coordinator Seth Ryan. He said his frustration comes from wanting to win, not from wanting the ball, and that he has not asked to be traded. Wilson, who signed a four-year, $130 million extension in 2025, still leads the team with 37 catches for 444 yards and three touchdowns, but has never had a winning season since New York drafted him in 2022. The NFL trade deadline is Nov. 10, and the Jets host Kirk Cousins and the Raiders on Sunday.

stories.headline: Putin calls Elon Musk 'a real genius' and says Moscow is in contact with him on space, days after Ukraine's Starshield came back
stories.summary: Vladimir Putin praised Elon Musk on Wednesday during an exhibition visit at the Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow, saying "Elon Musk is a genius, a real genius" as Russia scrambles to build its own answer to Starlink. Putin said that "despite all political issues" Moscow keeps in contact with its "U.S. partners, including Mr. Musk" on space matters, and that Roscosmos and other companies are working together. The remarks came less than a week after Ukraine restored full-speed use of commercial Starlink terminals and the military Starshield version following a restriction that began Oct. 14 and capped terminal speeds in a way that hampered Ukrainian drone interceptors. Musk has accused Ukraine of breaking the terms of service by using commercial terminals for offensive drone strikes, which Kyiv denies; neither Musk nor the Trump administration has claimed responsibility for the throttling.

stories.headline: RFK Jr.'s HHS will let small compounding pharmacies make six popular wellness peptides the FDA never approved
stories.summary: The Department of Health and Human Services says it will use "enforcement discretion" for six peptides, in effect letting small 503A compounding pharmacies make them even though the FDA has not approved them. Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has long backed wider access and says he has used some peptides himself. Peptides, short chains of amino acids promoted by wellness influencers for many uses, have been sold on a gray market as "research-use-only" products often sourced from overseas, and HHS argues compounding is a safer option. An FDA advisory panel voted in July to allow compounding of the six, though the agency's own scientists recommended against it. Pharmacists warn the small shops covered by the policy won't be able to meet demand, and the larger 503B outsourcing facilities are excluded. Consumer groups such as Public Citizen say the move puts patients at risk and skipped normal rulemaking.

stories.headline: Florida man charged with murder 15 years after his ex-fiancée vanished hours after their 'People's Court' taping
stories.summary: Orlando police have charged Dale Smith Jr., 55, with second-degree murder in the 2011 disappearance of Michelle Parker, his ex-fiancée and the mother of his twins, whose body has never been found. Court documents unsealed Tuesday say a fresh look at cellphone data and texts broke the case. On Nov. 17, 2011, the two taped an episode of "The People's Court" over a $5,000 engagement ring she allegedly threw off a balcony; the judge told them to split the cost. Smith said Parker dropped off the kids and left within 10 minutes, but surveillance video showed her Hummer at his home for at least an hour, and both of their phones then left together heading west, away from the mall her phone later texted that she was at. Investigators note Smith never called or messaged her again after that day. He was arrested Oct. 14, and police say he has a history of domestic violence.

stories.headline: Trumbull weekend: Halloween dance party and trick-or-treating at Trumbull Mall on Friday night
stories.summary: Trumbull Mall is throwing a costume party the night before Halloween, with a DJ, music, games, crafts and trick-or-treating for the whole family on Friday evening, Oct. 30. Patch's weekend guide for Trumbull suggests bringing the kids in costume for a Halloween warm-up the night before the holiday.

stories.headline: Trumbull this week: early voting’s final week at the library, a Town Hall Halloween parade for preschoolers, and a Hillcrest update
stories.summary: Early voting runs its final week in the Trumbull Library Community Room, 33 Quality St., from Monday, Oct. 26, through Sunday, Nov. 1. Hours are 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., extended to 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on Tuesday and Thursday. Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3, with polls open 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. On Tuesday, Oct. 27, at 10 and 11:30 a.m., Town Hall staff host a costume parade and trick-or-treating past decorated office doors for registered Trumbull kids ages 0 to 5. Each session is limited to 20 children. That evening the Hillcrest Middle School Building Committee gets project updates and the EMS Commission reviews vehicles, staffing and plans for Trumbull EMS’s 50th anniversary. The Conservation Commission meets Wednesday on tree rules and a spring 2027 tree giveaway.
